title: Private club proposed for residential block of Gay Street goes to zoning board Nov. 18
summary: The 1978 Phoenix Foundation is asking the Zoning Hearing Board for a special exception to run a private club and community center, plus a variance for office use, at 315 Gay St. in the Residential Infill District. The hearing is 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Borough Hall, and the application can be inspected there.

title: Valley Forge park draws nearly 800,000 summer visitors in record tourism year
summary: At its Oct. 29 annual luncheon, the Valley Forge Tourism & Convention Board reported record summer visitation at Valley Forge National Historical Park during its 50th year as a national park. Visitor spending in Montgomery County reached $1.8 billion in 2025, and hotels are on pace for about $300 million in room revenue this year.
loc: Valley Forge National Historical Park, Valley Forge

title: Main Street funeral home fire ruled not suspicious
summary: Fire officials say the Oct. 30 blaze on the third floor of Devlin-Gatcha Funeral Home was not suspicious. Crews spent about two and a half hours on scene and no one was hurt; the county fire marshal is still investigating.

title: Avlos joins Main Line Today Restaurant Week through Nov. 14
summary: Phoenixville's Avlos Greek Cuisine is among nearly 40 restaurants serving three- and four-course prix-fixe menus for the magazine's two-week promotion, which runs Nov. 1-14. Lunch menus run $25 to $35 and dinners $30 to $55, before tax, tip and drinks.

title: Phoenixville schools steer families to food help during SNAP disruption
summary: The Phoenixville Area School District issued a food-security notice pointing affected households to free school breakfast, meal-aid applications, the PACS pantry and Ann's Heart. Its Phoenixville Phamily Fund with Ann's Heart can also cover emergency food and shelter needs.

title: Route 23 safety rebuild through Phoenixville wraps up
summary: PennDOT says major construction is finished on its $2.5 million project covering 11 signalized intersections on Nutt Road, Schuylkill Road and Valley Forge Road in the borough, East Pikeland and Schuylkill Township. The work added a left-turn lane at Township Line Road and reconfigured the Nutt Road and Bridge Street intersection; brief single-lane closures continue for finishing touches.

title: Bed Races roll down Third Avenue at Reeves Park on Saturday, Nov. 7
summary: Teams push decorated beds on wheels from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., with a $1-a-vote Best Bed Theme contest until noon and the racing heats starting at noon. The day raises money for Ann's Heart and Good Samaritan Services, with food from local eateries, kids' crafts and face painting alongside the course.
loc: Third Avenue at Reeves Park, Phoenixville

title: Chicken Salad Chick sets Nov. 18 opening at Providence Town Center
summary: The Southern fast-casual chain's first Philadelphia-area restaurant takes the former Z!Eats space and will seat 55, with free chicken salad for a year promised to the first 100 guests. The local franchise group plans six locations across Montgomery and Chester counties.
loc: 500 Broad St., Providence Town Center, Collegeville

title: State grant brings on-street EV chargers to Phoenixville
summary: PennDOT's $37 million round of federal charging awards for southeastern Pennsylvania includes $482,991 to Voltpost for 23 Level 2 on-street ports spread across Phoenixville, West Chester and Malvern. The region gains 515 public ports in all; sites, pricing and timing for the Phoenixville chargers have not been announced.

title: Super Wawa on Route 23 opens on the former Exxon site
summary: The long-awaited store at 799 Valley Forge Road in Schuylkill Township, just over the borough line, opened Oct. 22 with 10 gas pumps and a 24-hour convenience store. Traffic was the neighbors' main worry, and a Sheetz was approved for the former Royal Bank site nearby at nearly the same time.
